input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: Searches for audit, inspection, verification, records, usage-monitoring and premises-access language return nothing: the Agreement grants IBM no right to audit or verify Customer's usage, no right to inspect our books or premises, and no access to Customer systems. The only adjacent right is § 11.3, where IBM may "investigate potential violations" of the Customer content warranties, but that is an internal determination by IBM leading to its own remedies — it imposes no audit, on-site inspection or system-access obligation on us, so there is nothing for the audit parameters (frequency, notice, cost) to constrain. The position is therefore better than the preferred position and no redline is warranted. Noted only for the record: § 11.3's final paragraph requires Customer to provide relevant information about events that could lead to a claim against IBM at IBM's request; that is a claims-cooperation duty rather than an audit right, and is a minor sub-element handled under indemnity cooperation rather than this rule.
